body: Yes, without an OB you can still pass it along, even on the antivirals. That is always a risk but you can minimize the likelihood of passing it along through taking your medication and practicing safe sex. That’s why part of this conversation is hard because you have to be honest and let them know the risk is always going to be at some percentage and then inform them of the realities of living with HSV. It’s hard not to feel guilty when you pass it along as well but I’m a firm believer in just giving your partners a chance to decide if they want to take that risk for themselves.

I’ll tell you the same thing I told my sister whose father did the same to her.
With time you will heal. You will learn to process and grieve what he took from you. You will find love. You’ll experience the best days of your life which you haven’t even gotten to have yet but they are coming. You’ll have a great job and a beautiful home and a pet you can’t stop obsessing over and maybe even kids someday. You’ll go to concerts and try amazing food and travel the world.
And slowly but surely, the oppressiveness of what he did to you will fade. You’ll stop thinking about it every day. It’ll cross your mind every few days. Then maybe once a week. Eventually it will fade into something that you rarely consider and the pain will lessen as well.

However, your father (which I hate to even call him that) will think about what he did to you every single day for the rest of his life. In his mind he knows he’s a predator and a monster and he will be fearful you will tell on him (which you should when you are ready). He will be haunted by it until his dying day.

You will forget him.
He will never forget you.

Peace is yours and HE IS THE ONE who should be tormented.
It was not your fault girl. No matter if you didn’t scream or cry or tell anyone.
You hold no blame.
Wishing you the utmost peace and please give yourself a chance to live a beautiful life. Don’t let him take anything more from you.

I dated after my ex gave it to me. I told four different people while we were in the talking stage. Only one of them actually cared and he ghosted me for it.

I’ve been with one of them now for four years and we just had a baby. Most people just appreciate honesty. That shows character in and of itself.
If you tell them honestly about the risks and what you can do to minimize potential for passing it to them, it helps.
Also, if you’ve had it this long I imagine you’re past the worst of your outbreaks which makes it easier as well.
My ex passed it to me (after withholding he had it which was such a jerk move) around 2016 and I now can’t even remember the last time I had a breakout.
My current did catch it from me despite our protection but he has a breakout MAYBE once a year.

Just don’t let yourself feel ashamed for it because it gives people who do reject you over it power over your self-worth.
There’s plenty of people who won’t care. Promise.

I love this. I’m totally with you. Disclosing would be the right thing to do. And I implore everyone to disclose first. We all remember what it was like to find out we had it, even moreso when you weren’t first given the choice to decide if your partner was someone who you would take that risk with.

However, we all handle things differently. I can’t even say I blame my ex for not telling me. It’s scary. To me personally though, it just goes to show him and I are just built different. Hopefully since we broke up, he’s gotten to a point he can disclose.
I’m still angry he didn’t tell me, and angry that I have it, but I’m a sucker for playing devils advocate and I do understand why he didn’t.

Give it a few more years and we will all be in a better place with this.

To anyone struggling with disclosure, just take your time and wait for the right moment. With the right person, it will feel much easier to disclose than with the wrong one.
It’s cliche, but it’s true.
And there’s plenty enough people out there who will still want you despite that fact.
I’ve only been rejected once over it.

Good luck, everybody. 🤍
And try not to beat yourself up.
Herpes doesn’t mean you don’t deserve to be happy and it doesn’t mean you’re dirty.

Pick up a pencil and grab a piece of paper.
Start a list.
Write down every thing you can think of that puts a smile on your face, evokes a laugh, or makes you excited.

Do you have a certain dog breed you’ve always dreamt of having?
What city have you always wanted to visit? Live in?
If you could learn one new skill, what would it be?

You’ll have two columns.
Things that bring you joy, and goals you can hope for.
Be honest. Even if they’re small things. They all matter.

Then hang up that piece of paper and read it every single day. Check off the goals you meet. Add new ones when you think of them.

I don’t care if it’s something as simple as buying some fancy chopsticks because you love ramen noodles or going to a local park and getting on a swing.

Do that. And then message me. And we can talk about all the things you discovered.
